---
title: "NACDC: National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse"
description: "Information on people receiving aged care and the services and organisations providing care."

Information on people receiving aged care and the services and organisations providing care.

*Defines the clearinghouse, its aged-care populations, program coverage, periods and access.*

The AIHW defines the element as \"the person's date of entry into a service/facility\", and notes that \"when used combined with exit_date\" it \"provides dates for a continuity of service record\" - which is what separates it from ADMISSION_DATE on the residential table, where a move between place types inside one home starts a new admission but not a new entry. Everything measured in days for this collection, above all length of stay, is built from this date and EXIT_DATE.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. Read with ENTRY_CARE_LEVEL it says both what programme and at what level a person entered.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. The AIHW defines the concept as \"The reason recorded for discharge from aged care service on separation\", adding that these \"are effectively the person's destination on separation from aged care\", and groups them as hospital, transfer to residential aged care, transfer to community-based care, return to family or home, death, and other. The same column appears on the home care, residential care and transition care episode tables, so it is the field that reveals a pathway: a transition care episode ending in a transfer to residential care is a different outcome from one ending in a return home.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. The source systems behind it use a numbered list that separates hospital, residential aged care at low and high care, death, return to family or home, several return-to-community values distinguished by which programme picks the person up, recipient-initiated and provider-initiated endings, other and a system-generated auto value.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. The closest published national element, AIHW METEOR's aged care assessment setting, defines the concept as \"The setting in which an aged care assessment took place, as represented by a code\" and separates the person's home, a carer's home, another community setting, a residential care home, private and public hospitals, other inpatient settings and clinics. The setting is worth reading as a route into care rather than as a location: a hospital contact usually means a discharge-driven assessment, while a home contact usually means a community-initiated one.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 807741, 'Aged care assessment-assessment setting, code N[N]'","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/807741","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The setting where the person made the first face-to-face contact with the aged care assessment team as represented by text.","k":"aged care assessment setting","def":"A short text label naming a setting. The Transition Care Program guidelines make the measure explicit: \"The use of the Modified Barthel Index for assessments by the transition care registered providers at entry to and exit from the TCP is mandatory for Australian Government subsidy payments.\" That is the baseline against which the whole episode is judged, because transition care exists to restore function after a hospital stay, and the gain to FUNCTIONAL_CAPACITY_EXIT is the programme's central outcome measure.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Transition Care Program Guidelines (June 2026), section 4.2.1","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-07/transition-care-program-guidelines_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Functional capacity score (between 0-100) of the recipient at time of entry to transition care","k":"Modified Barthel Index score (0 to 100)","def":"An integer from 0 to 100 on the Modified Barthel Index, a ten-item rating of activities of daily living covering feeding, bathing, grooming, dressing, bowel and bladder control, toilet use, transfers, mobility and stairs. It is a payment-driven record of a diagnosis rather than a clinical one, entering the collection through the supplement claim rather than through any health dataset.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Aged Care Subsidies and Supplements (rates of payments effective at 1 January 2025)","url":"https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-01/schedule-of-subsidies-and-supplements-for-aged-care_0.pdf","lim":"It is not a dementia register. The department describes leave as the situation where a person stops receiving services for a while without giving up their place, and the rules differ by programme: in residential care the reasons are a hospital stay, transition care, social reasons or a declared emergency, while in home care a person can pause for a hospital stay, transition care, residential respite or social reasons. Because a leave row sits inside an episode rather than closing it, subtracting leave days is what turns time enrolled into time actually served.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Managing temporary leave for residential aged care","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/our-work/residential-aged-care/managing/managing-temporary-leave","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Start date of leave","k":"date","def":"A calendar date. AIHW METEOR defines the national element as \"Whether a person usually resides alone or with others, as represented by a code\", with the list 1 lives alone, 2 lives with family, 3 lives with others and 9 not stated or inadequately described. In aged care it is one of the strongest predictors on the record of whether someone can be supported at home, because living alone removes the informal care a co-resident partner or child would otherwise supply.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 270385, 'Person-living arrangement, code N'","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/270385","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Identifies the living arrangements of the client.","k":"living arrangement code","def":"A single-digit code or its label, resolving to lives alone, lives with family, lives with others, or a not stated value. MARITAL_STATUS_DESC on the same row is the label. In aged care the field carries weight beyond demography, because a partner is often the informal carer whose availability decides whether someone can stay at home.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 291045, 'Person-marital status, code N'","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/291045","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Marital status of the recipient (at time of assessment)","k":"marital status code","def":"A single-digit code. Group on the code and display this column, since the labels are what change between collections while the codes do not.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 291045, 'Person-marital status, code N'","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/291045","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Marital status code of person as represented by text.","k":"marital status label","def":"Short text: never married, widowed, divorced, separated, married including de facto, or a not stated value. OUTLET_STATE and OUTLET_SA2_CODE_2016 beside it are the same outlet at coarser and finer geography, while RECIPIENT_POSTCODE on the client table is the person's own address.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AIHW METEOR defines the national element as \"The language (including sign language) most preferred by the person for communication, as represented by a code\", and notes that this \"may be a language other than English even where the person can speak fluent English\". The AIHW records preferred language as a separate element from main language spoken at home and as one available only through the recipient table, so it is the aged care system's own record of communication need rather than a household characteristic.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 659407, 'Person-preferred language, code (ASCL 2016) N[NNN]'","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/index.phtml/itemId/659407","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Code of language the recipient prefers to speak","k":"Australian Standard Classification of Languages (ASCL) language code","def":"A numeric code of up to four digits from the Australian Standard Classification of Languages, built as a three-level hierarchy: one digit for a broad group, two or three for a narrow group and four for a specific language. It is what groups the many services on aged_service under one owner, and what ties a home support episode back to the body that was paid for it. SERVICE_ID_ENCRYPTED is the finer key: one provider can hold many services.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80","url":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","lim":"It identifies an approved provider, not a corporate group or a brand, so a chain operating under several approvals looks like several unrelated providers, and a merger or a change of approval breaks one operator's history in two. The AIHW defines the concept as the \"Type of organisation providing aged care services through a national aged care program\" and groups the values as not-for-profit, covering charitable, community-based and religious organisations, private, covering for-profit and incorporated companies, and government, covering local, state and territory bodies. It is the standard breakdown for almost every published figure about who delivers aged care, and it appears on both the service table and the home support episode table so provision can be split by sector at either level.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. It sits with PROVIDER_ID_ENCRYPTED, PROVIDER_ORGANISATION_TYPE and PROVIDER_INCORPORATED_BODY, all of which describe the corporate entity rather than the care, and it also appears on the CHSP session table for the grant-funded home support provider. That matters because the AIHW refreshes history at every supply: \"Each annual supply also refreshes data from previous years where records have been revised or updated\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024), so one episode can appear in several vintages with different values, and this column is how you choose which one you are reading.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024","durl":"https://www.gen-agedcaredata.gov.au/getmedia/fcc6d59b-fb72-4066-841d-95eb4a67cbea/NACDC-user-guide-July-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The latest date for which data in this table is available. this will be updated with each data supply.","k":"date (extract currency date)","def":"A single calendar date, identical on every row of a table. Whether it also locates the people is a question of program: the AIHW states that \"The location of people using permanent residential care is the same as the service location. It is a single postcode for a service that may cover a whole region, and it gives no radius, no boundary and no measure of how far people travel. Postcode areas are also mail rounds, so they do not nest inside the SA2 in the next column.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_SA2_CODE","d":"The small statistical area containing the aged care facility or outlet, which is the unit AIHW aged care reporting uses to compare service supply across the country.","full":"The small statistical area containing the aged care facility or outlet, which is the unit AIHW aged care reporting uses to compare service supply across the country. SERVICE_SA2_NAME on the same row is the label for this code and carries no extra information. Because the NACDC geocodes most programs by service location rather than recipient location, this is the column that drives supply-side measures such as places per head of older population, while RECIPIENT_SA2_CODE_2016 on the CHSP recipient tables is the only demand-side equivalent in the dataset.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"The australian statistical geography standard statistical area level 2 identifier related to the physical address of the aged care service as represented by a code.","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A nine digit fully hierarchical code: one digit for the state or territory, then the SA4, SA3 and four digit SA2 identifiers. The ABS defines the areas themselves as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1\" that \"represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\".","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","lim":"The ASGS edition is not stated in the metadata, unlike RECIPIENT_SA2_CODE_2016 on the CHSP tables, so the codes cannot safely be assumed to match those and should be checked against a boundary file before any join to Census or population denominators. Beyond that, an SA2 is not a catchment: a residential facility draws residents from well beyond its own area, and a home care outlet's clients are scattered across many SA2s, so a count of services by SA2 measures where providers are registered, not where care is consumed.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_SA2_NAME","d":"The readable label for the statistical area holding the aged care facility or outlet, and the same fact as SERVICE_SA2_CODE beside it.","full":"The readable label for the statistical area holding the aged care facility or outlet, and the same fact as SERVICE_SA2_CODE beside it. Its only advantage is that it needs no lookup, which is why it is worth using for a table heading or a map label and not for a join. The area it names is a community-sized ABS region built from whole SA1s, so it usually reads like a suburb or a group of suburbs even though it is neither.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The australian statistical geography standard statistical area level 2 identifier related to the physical address of the aged care service as represented by text.","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 name","def":"The ABS name of an SA2, as text. SA2s are redrawn between ASGS editions and names are added, retired and reused, so joining datasets on the text will silently drop rows and merge areas that are not the same; the code column, with a known edition, is the safe key. The name also encourages a second error — reading an SA2 as a suburb. It is a statistical area that frequently spans several suburbs or splits one, so it will not agree with a suburb-level address list.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_STATE","d":"The state or territory in which the aged care facility or outlet physically sits, as a name rather than a code.","full":"The state or territory in which the aged care facility or outlet physically sits, as a name rather than a code. It is the level at which most published aged care supply figures are broken down, and it is unaffected by ASGS boundary changes, unlike the SA2 columns on the same row, so it is the safest way to group services over a long run of extracts. It can differ from PROVIDER_STATE on the same row whenever a provider operates across borders.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024","durl":"https://www.gen-agedcaredata.gov.au/getmedia/fcc6d59b-fb72-4066-841d-95eb4a67cbea/NACDC-user-guide-July-2024","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"State or territory name for the physical address of a service","k":"Australian state or territory name","def":"A state or territory as text, from the standard set of the six states, the two internal territories and other territories. The AIHW code set behind those names reserves further values for not applicable and not stated; this column holds the name only.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METEOR value domain 787653, 'Australian state/territory code N[N]'","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/787653","lim":"Aged care is Commonwealth funded, so the state here is a location and not a funder, a regulator or a policy boundary; state differences in this dataset reflect where facilities were built, not different programmes. The AIHW defines the underlying concept as \"The operational status of places, services and providers\" and notes that \"While other codes for status exist in source data, NACDC commonly only reports on operational places, services or providers\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary), so in a NACDC extract this column is close to constant and its real job is to let you drop the services that were never open. Read it with SERVICE_TOTAL_PLACES, since only an operating service has operational places behind that count.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","durl":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The operational status of the aged care service as represented by text.","k":"aged care service operational status (text)","def":"Short status labels as text, derived in the source systems from a service status code. The parallel place-level concept in NACDC divides allocations into operational places, unused or offline places and provisionally allocated places, and the service-level status is the same idea applied to the whole outlet.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","url":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","lim":"It is a status at one instant, not a history, so it cannot date an opening or a closure; a facility that shut halfway through the year still shows a single value in the extract, and only the gap in the episode tables reveals when it stopped taking residents. It is also not a quality signal: it says the service is operating, not that it is accredited, compliant or performing, and none of the sanction and accreditation information published elsewhere by the regulator is in this column.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_SUBTYPE_DESC","d":"The finest description of what was actually delivered at a home support session: podiatry rather than allied health, garden maintenance rather than home maintenance, visiting rather than social support.","full":"The finest description of what was actually delivered at a home support session: podiatry rather than allied health, garden maintenance rather than home maintenance, visiting rather than social support. It is the third level of the Commonwealth Home Support Programme service list that ran until 30 June 2025, sitting under SERVICE_TYPE_DESC and SERVICE_TYPE_CODE on the same row. Since the chsp_episode tables cover 2017 to 2024, every value here belongs to that old list, which the Department rebuilt for the Aged Care Act 2024.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP) Service List Mapping Guide, June 2025","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/commonwealth-home-support-program-chsp-service-list-mapping.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Type of home support service (service subtype) as represented by text.","k":"CHSP service sub-type (pre-July 2025 service list)","def":"Text names from the pre-1 July 2025 CHSP service sub-type list, which sat beneath a service type, which in turn sat beneath one of three services — community and home support, assistance with care and housing, and care relationships and carer support. Examples run from podiatry, physiotherapy and exercise physiology under allied health and therapy services, through garden maintenance and minor home maintenance and repairs, to direct and indirect transport.","p":"2016 to current","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP) Service List Mapping Guide, June 2025","url":"https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/commonwealth-home-support-program-chsp-service-list-mapping.pdf","lim":"The sub-type detail is uneven and cannot be treated as a clean taxonomy. Several service types carried catch-all sub-types such as other allied health and therapy services and other goods and equipment, which the Department retired in 2025 and replaced with a requirement that providers report the actual service delivered, so a sub-type distribution understates specific services and overstates residual ones. Values also do not map one-to-one onto the post-2025 service names, so a time series that crosses 1 July 2025 needs the Department's mapping tables rather than a string match.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2017","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2018","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2019","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2020","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2021","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2022","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2023","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_2024","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_jun2017","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_jun2018","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_jun2019","madipge-aged-care-d-chsp-16-current / chsp_episode_jun2020","and 3 more"]},{"n":"SERVICE_TOTAL_PLACES","d":"How big the service is, measured in government-funded places — beds in a residential facility, packages in a home care outlet — as at 30 June of the previous financial year.","full":"How big the service is, measured in government-funded places — beds in a residential facility, packages in a home care outlet — as at 30 June of the previous financial year. The AIHW defines the size of a service as \"the number of operational places available through the outlet/facility\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary), and this is the standard size measure in aged care reporting, used to build supply ratios against the older population of SERVICE_SA2_CODE. It is capacity, and the episode tables are the only place to find out whether that capacity was used.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","durl":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The number of aged care places applied to the aged care service for the previous financial year (as at 30 june).","k":"count of allocated aged care places (integer)","def":"A whole number of places. Places are the packages or beds allocated to a service or provider and are the standard measure of system capacity; an allocation is made up of operational places, unused or offline places and provisionally allocated places, and this count is the operational allocation as at the previous 30 June.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","url":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","lim":"It is capacity, not occupancy, and service-level occupancy rates are not published, so a large number here does not mean a large caseload. It is also blind to composition: residential places do not distinguish permanent from respite, and have not distinguished low from high care since 1 July 2014. The gap that catches people out is home care — places have not been reportable for the Home Care Packages Program since 27 February 2017, because funding follows the recipient rather than the outlet, so a busy home care service can show no places at all. Finally the figure is an as-at-30-June value for the previous financial year while the rest of the row is current to REFERENCE_DATE, so the two are not aligned in time.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_TYPE","d":"The aged care programme the service operates under.","full":"The aged care programme the service operates under. The AIHW defines the matching concept as the \"Type of aged care program\", derived from the service type code and \"broadly categorised as: Residential, Community, Transition Care\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary). Treat the description carried in the PLIDA data item list with suspicion: it defines a child care service and has been mapped onto this column by mistake, so nothing in it applies to aged care. The column pairs with SERVICE_APPROVAL_CARE_TYPE, which is the specific care type the service is approved to deliver, and it is the field the NACDC derives its published programme type from.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","durl":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The main type of activity available from or provided by the child care service or provider attended by the child","k":"aged care program type (text)","def":"Text programme labels. The AIHW's programme type concept, which it derives from the service type code, is \"broadly categorised as: Residential, Community, Transition Care\", and the modern programme set in the NACDC covers home support, home care, residential care, flexible care and aged care eligibility assessments.","p":"2015 to current","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, version 1.0, 2016","url":"https://www.aihw.gov.au/getmedia/a8d4f12e-c90c-4de3-a502-9fdfac21ebef/20344.pdf.aspx?inline=true","lim":"It is the programme a service is funded under, not the mix of care it delivers, and it does not give a care level — Home Care Package levels 1 to 4 and the AN-ACC classifications live with the person, not the service. Its greatest risk is the wrong description shipped alongside it, which invites a reader to interpret aged care rows as child care.","where":["madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_apr2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jan2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2024","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_jun2025","madipge-aged-care-d-agedservice-15-current / aged_service_oct2024"]},{"n":"SERVICE_TYPE_CODE","d":"The Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type delivered in this episode, such as domestic assistance, meals, nursing or transport.","full":"The Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type delivered in this episode, such as domestic assistance, meals, nursing or transport. The CHSP classification has three levels, service, service type and service sub-type, and SERVICE_TYPE_DESC and SERVICE_SUBTYPE_DESC on the same row carry the labels while this column carries the internal code. It is the field that gives the volume columns their meaning, because ASSISTANCE_MINUTES_NBR, ASSISTANCE_QUANTITY_NBR and ASSISTANCE_COST_AMT are all measured per service type.","dsrc":"Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP) Service List Mapping, June 2025","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/commonwealth-home-support-program-chsp-service-list-mapping.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Code for type of service","k":"Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type, pre-1 July 2025 service list (inferred; internal code values not published)","def":"A short internal code, one per service type on the pre-1 July 2025 CHSP service list of 17 client-facing types. It is the label that defines the session itself, because the AIHW records CHSP activity so that \"A session represents the services provided to one or more people by a service outlet, for a particular day and a particular service type\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024). SERVICE_TYPE_CODE on the same row is the coded form of this value and SERVICE_SUBTYPE_DESC breaks it down further, so a person receiving three kinds of help in a week appears on three rows.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024","durl":"https://www.gen-agedcaredata.gov.au/getmedia/fcc6d59b-fb72-4066-841d-95eb4a67cbea/NACDC-user-guide-July-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Description for type of service","k":"CHSP service type (pre-July 2025 service list)","def":"Text names from the Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type list in force before 1 July 2025. Home support is recorded differently from the rest of aged care: \"CHSP episodes are collected per provision of service, or 'session', while home care, residential care and flexible care episodes are collected per entry into care, or 'admission'\" (National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024), so where rac_episode and hcp_episode have entry and exit dates, this table has one date per delivery. Combined with SERVICE_TYPE_DESC it builds a person's pattern of home support across a year, and it is the only way to see frequency or gaps.","dsrc":"AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse: User guide, July 2024","durl":"https://www.gen-agedcaredata.gov.au/getmedia/fcc6d59b-fb72-4066-841d-95eb4a67cbea/NACDC-user-guide-July-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date session was conducted","k":"date","def":"A calendar date, held in the NACDC's day, month and year form.
